name: wealthstoryline
description: Retirement and savings Monte Carlo simulator: household income, living expenses, savings and investment returns under random inflation, salary growth and market returns. Supports about 190 countries (curated data for Taiwan, Japan, US, China and Canada).

interface.longDescription:
WealthStoryLine runs a 3,000-path Monte Carlo simulation of a household's finances: one household income, living expenses, today's savings and investment returns, under random inflation, salary growth and market returns. Ask questions such as "Can I retire at 60?", "Will my savings last?" or "Can I reach $500,000 by 45?" and get the probability of reaching your goal, the bankruptcy rate and net-asset ranges for good, middle and bad outcomes in today's money, together with the assumptions that were used.

Who it is for: individuals, couples and financial educators who want to check a plan and its risks in plain language. It supports about 190 countries; Taiwan, Japan, the US, China and Canada use curated assumptions, other countries use 2005-2024 averages of official statistics (World Bank, OECD, BIS).

No sign-in is required. The plugin receives only the numbers needed for a simulation, not your conversation; anonymous inputs and results are deleted after 30 days.

Limitations: results are projections for planning discussions, not financial advice or a guarantee. Home purchases, mortgages, several incomes and fund portfolios are not modelled in this plugin (they are available on the WealthStoryLine website). Taxes and insurance are not modelled. It cannot trade, move money or connect to bank or brokerage accounts.
defaultPrompt: Can I retire at 60 with $200k saved, $120k income and $70k yearly spending?
Will $500k last if I retire at 55 and spend $40k a year?
How likely am I to reach $1 million by 50?

positive.prompt: I'm 40 and live in the US. I have $200,000 saved, earn $120,000 a year and spend $70,000. I want to retire at 60 with a $24,000 pension and have $1 million by then. Will it work?
positive.expected_behavior: Runs a quick US simulation and reports the probability of reaching $1 million by age 60 (about 98% in testing), net-asset ranges for good, middle and bad outcomes, and states that the default 8% investment return was assumed.

positive.prompt: I'm 50 in Taiwan with NT$8 million saved. I earn NT$1.5 million and spend NT$800,000 a year. If I retire at 60 with a NT$300,000 pension, will my money last?
positive.expected_behavior: Runs a Taiwan simulation in TWD. With no target given it uses 25x annual spending (NT$20 million) by age 60 as a reference goal and says so; reports about a 55% chance of reaching it, a bankruptcy rate under 1%, and net-asset ranges after retirement.

positive.prompt: What inflation, salary growth and house price assumptions do you use for Germany?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Germany's defaults in EUR from official statistics (2005-2024 averages): inflation about 2.0%, salary growth about 2.7%, house prices about 3.0%, base rate about 1.3%, each with its standard deviation and source (World Bank CPI, OECD wages, BIS policy rate and residential property prices).

positive.prompt: I'm 30 in Canada with $50,000 saved, earn $90,000 and spend $60,000 a year. How likely am I to have $500,000 by 45?
positive.expected_behavior: Runs a Canada simulation in CAD and reports about a 94% chance of reaching $500,000 by age 45, with net-asset ranges and the default 8% investment return it assumed.

positive.prompt: How does the WealthStoryLine simulation work and what doesn't it model?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains the 3,000-path Monte Carlo method, the outputs, and the main limitations: taxes and insurance are not modelled and results are projections, not advice.

negative.description: Trading request: the plugin cannot place orders
negative.prompt: Buy $5,000 of VOO in my brokerage account.

negative.description: Stock tip: the plugin does not pick investments or predict prices
negative.prompt: Which stock will double my money this year?

negative.description: Account access: the plugin cannot connect to bank or brokerage accounts
negative.prompt: Log in to my bank and import my account balances.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. All simulation features are currently free.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: quick household retirement and savings Monte Carlo simulation for about 190 countries, country assumptions and methodology.

zh-TW.subtitle: 退休與財富模擬器
zh-TW.description: 財富故事線用 3,000 條蒙地卡羅路徑，模擬一個家庭的收入、生活支出、現有存款與投資報酬，並考慮通膨、薪資成長與市場報酬的隨機變化。可以問「60 歲能退休嗎？」「存款夠用到老嗎？」「45 歲前存得到 50 萬嗎？」，得到達成目標的機率、破產率，以及好中壞三種情境的淨資產（以今天的幣值表示）。支援約 190 個國家。不需登入，只接收模擬需要的數字，匿名資料 30 天後刪除。本外掛不模擬買房、房貸、多份收入與基金組合（官網有）；也不模擬稅與保險，不能下單或連結銀行帳戶。結果僅供規劃討論，不構成投資建議。

ja-JP.subtitle: 退職・資産シミュレーター
ja-JP.description: WealthStoryLineは3,000通りのモンテカルロ・シミュレーションで、世帯の収入、生活費、現在の貯蓄と投資リターンを、インフレ、昇給、市場リターンの変動を含めて試算します。「60歳で退職できる？」「貯蓄は足りる？」などの質問に対し、目標達成の確率、破綻率、良い・中間・悪いケースの純資産（現在価値）を表示します。約190か国に対応。ログイン不要で、試算に必要な数値のみを受け取り、匿名データは30日後に削除します。住宅購入、住宅ローン、複数の収入、ファンドの組み合わせは本プラグインでは扱いません（ウェブサイトで利用可能）。税金と保険は対象外で、売買や口座連携はできません。結果は計画検討用の予測であり、投資助言ではありません。
